entities.summary: Rouben V. Ambartzumian is an Armenian mathematician and Academician of National Academy of Sciences of Armenia. He works in Stochastic Geometry and Integral Geometry where he created a new branch, combinatorial integral geometry. The subject of combinatorial integral geometry received support from mathematicians K. Krickeberg and D. G. Kendall at the 1976 Sevan Symposium (Armenia) which was sponsored by Royal Society of London and The London Mathematical Society. In the framework of the later theory he solved a number of classical problems in particular the solution to the Buffon Sylvester problem as well as Hilbert's fourth problem in 1976.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Rouben Ambartzumian's work on combinatorial integral geometry contributed to solving classical problems in probability theory, including the Buffon Sylvester problem and Hilbert's fourth problem. His research has had a lasting impact on the field of stochastic geometry.
